atoms.text: Ellis Island is an island in New York. It is located next to the Statue of Liberty. Ellis Island is named after a merchant who bought the island in the 1770s. From 1892 to 1924, Ellis Island was the largest immigration station in the USA. Millions of people passed through it. Today, Ellis Island is a museum.

atoms.text: This is Annie Moore. She was born in Ireland in 1874. Annie grew up with her parents Matthew and Julia, as well as her three brothers.

In the 19th century, people in Ireland suffered from economic problems as well as several famines. In 1888, Annie's parents and her older brother decided to migrate from Ireland to New York, USA. They were hoping for a better life abroad. Annie and her two younger brothers had to stay in Ireland because the family wasn't able to afford passage for everyone.

atoms.text:
After their parents found work in New York, they sent tickets to Annie and her brothers. With these tickets, they got on a ship, the S.S. Nevada, to America.
Annie and her brothers travelled in third class. That means that they didn't have a very comfortable passage. They stayed in a crammed area of the ship and didn't have much food.

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>comfortable:</lang> bedeutet gemütlich. <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>crammed:</lang> bedeutet überfüllt.

atoms.text: On New Year's Eve 1891, the S.S. Nevada arrived at Ellis Island in New York. The next day, the passengers of 3rd class were allowed to leave the ship. Annie Moore was the first officially registered immigrant at Ellis Island and was gifted $10 as a welcome gift from America. Annie and her brothers were later reunited with the rest of their family.

atoms.a: Annie Moore was the first person to come to America.
Annie's parents migrated from Ireland to America in hope of a better life.
Annie and her brothers were travelling in 1st class on the S.S. Nevada.
Annie Moore was gifted $10 as a welcome gift from America.

atoms.text: Ellis Island was known as not only the island of hope but also as the island of tears. While many people who passed through the famous immigration station were able to start a new life in America, others were sent back to their home countries.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody rate = '90%'>Ellis Island was known as not only the island of hope but also as the island of tears. While many people who passed through the famous immigration station were able to start a new life in America, others were sent back to their home countries.</prosody>

atoms.text: People who travelled in 1st or 2nd class were often allowed to immigrate immediately. This happened because officials thought that rich people had access to better healthcare and thus don't get sick. People who travelled in 3rd class were treated differently. Having only little money meant that they could not afford good health care. They were tested for cholera and typhus. If a person was sick, they were not allowed to stay in America.

atoms.a: Did all people who arrived at Ellis Island get to live in America?
b: ++No, some people were sent back to their home countries.
No, all people were sent back to their home countries.
Yes, all people passed through and got to live in America.

atoms.a: Why were 1st and 2nd class passengers treated differently from 3rd class passengers?
b: Officials thought that rich people get sick, because they couldn't afford healthcare.
Officials thought that poor people don't get sick, because they couldn't afford healthcare.
++Officials thought that rich people don't get sick, because they could afford healthcare.
